written: 2026-11-19, after SeedLM-8, before s9-early was trained
motivation: In all five recent coders' training curves (first 60 examples of each held-out set at 30, 60 and 90 minutes), held-out teacher tasks and real held-out programs are best at the first checkpoint and then decline while the synthetic set keeps improving (reports/seedlm/seedlm8_protocol.json, outcome). The small sources are repeated 20 to 95 times; after about half an hour the coder overfits them, and the coder used is always the one at the end of training
hypothesis: A checkpoint chosen during training by rows held out from the training sources themselves is better on held-out tasks than the end-of-training coder of the same run
coder: s9-early: scripts/seedlm4_train.py --name s9-early --minutes 120 --variant-share 0.1 --graft-share 0.1 --compose-share 0.1 --internal-val --checkpoint-minutes 15 (s8-all's mix). A twentieth of the training tasks (real rows, teacher tasks, composed tasks, by a hash of the task id) is kept out of training; every 15 training minutes the coder's top-1 reproduce rate on up to 100 rows of each is averaged, and the best checkpoint (ties: the earlier) is saved as s9-early, the end of training as s9-early-last. No measurement set is used to choose. Nothing else runs on the machine while it trains
primary_measure: held-out teacher tasks (139), first verified program at width 32 correct on all three cases (scripts/seedlm5_fragments.py): s9-early against s9-early-last. Supported if at least 5 more; inconclusive at 1 to 4 more; not supported otherwise. If the best checkpoint is the last one, the hypothesis is not supported by construction
secondary_measures: the same against s5-var (52) and s8-all (62)
held-out development fifth: pyx_model and the best method for both checkpoints (s5-var 57 and 69, s8-all 53 and 67), and engine failures solved by pyx_model
end-of-training metrics of both checkpoints: real held-out programs, held-out composed tasks, beyond
choice: s9-early replaces s5-var only if its best method solves more of the held-out development fifth than 69; then the validation gate (alone no fewer than the engine's 19 of 45; in the 1.5B pipeline no fewer than 31), one MBPP+ test run and one HumanEval+ run
not_tuned_on: the held-out teacher tasks and development fifth
note_1: The first s9-early run stopped after 60 training minutes: the data-segment cap that training then set (12 GB) refused an ordinary 208 MB allocation. No measurement had run; its four internal-validation scores were 0.643, 0.642, 0.665 and 0.675 at 15, 30, 45 and 60 minutes. The cap was removed from training (commit 08edf8f) and the run was started again with the same arguments
note_2: The second run was stopped at 52 training minutes by a restart of the machine; no measurement had run. Its internal scores at 15, 30 and 45 minutes were 0.673, 0.758 and 0.630, against the first run's 0.643, 0.642 and 0.665 with the same arguments: on 256 rows the score moves by up to 0.1 between runs. The third run scores every internal row (up to 200 per source, about 440 rows) instead of 100 per source, to make the choice less noisy; nothing else changes

outcome.written: 2026-11-20, after the pre-registered measures of the third run
outcome.selection: internal scores at 15, 30, 45, 60, 75, 90 and 105 minutes: 0.710, 0.734, 0.614, 0.649, 0.692, 0.683, 0.654; the 30-minute checkpoint (step 1,490 of 5,901) was chosen
outcome.primary: held-out teacher tasks, first verified at width 32: s9-early 57, s9-early-last 53 (+4): inconclusive by the pre-registered rule (supported needed +5). New compositions 20 vs 18, all pieces seen 37 vs 35

secondary.against_earlier: s5-var 52, s8-all 62: the same mix as s8-all ended at 53 in this run (5,901 steps on a faster machine, a twentieth of the tasks held out), so run-to-run differences of this measure reach 9
secondary.end_of_training: the chosen checkpoint is better on every held-out set by the coder's own top-1: real held-out programs 74.7% vs 60.0%, held-out teacher tasks 54.0% vs 46.0%, held-out composed tasks 45.5% vs 36.6%, with lower losses; synthetic 85.7% vs 93.0%; beyond 4 and 4
secondary.held_out_development: s9-early: pyx_model 53, best 68 (pyx_tie_fill); s9-early-last: pyx_model 54, best 68 (pyx_tie, pyx_tie_fill); engine failures solved by pyx_model 4 and 4

outcome.choice: best method 68, not more than 69: not adopted
outcome.reading: Choosing the checkpoint removes most of the overfitting the coder's own metrics show, but those metrics count programs that reproduce the visible example, and the gain shrinks to +4 when correctness on all cases is counted and to nothing on the development fifth. The two s8-all-mix runs (62 and 53) show that a single run cannot resolve differences of this size
